newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BRL Hardy sees double-digit sales growth.
newsitem.headline: BRL Hardy sees double-digit sales growth.

text.p: Vintner and wine-maker BRL Hardy Ltd said on Thursday it had experienced double-digit domestic sales growth in the first quarter of 1997, in line with its expectations.

"Sales in 1997 have continue to grow. In Australia, our domestic sales and marketing teams have achieved double digit percentage sales increases in the first quarter, while Australian exports over the same period have continued to exceed industry growth," Chairman John Pendrigh told the annual meeting. "This has been a good start to the year and we remain confident that 1997 will see good growth levels maintained."
Pendrigh said the 1997 vintage would be a good quality one, even if volumes would be down about 10 percent on 1996.
"Our winemakers had identified a number of parcels of exceptional fruit and are very pleased with the overall quality of fruit intake," he said.
BRL Hardy was aware that organic growth would not be enough to meet the company's needs into the future.
"Acquisitions, joint ventures and strategic alliances are a key part of our growth strategies and remain under constant review," Pendrigh said.
He referred to BRL Hardy's joint venture with Nobilo Vintners and its strategic alliance with Brian McGuigan Wines as examples of such joint ventures and alliances.
"Some other interesting opportunities are being considered by management at the present time."
He did not give any further details.
BRL Hardy has previously said it was comfortable with analysts' forecasts of a profit of about A$23.5 million in calendar 1997, up from the A$21.2 million recorded in 1996.
It had also said it was targetting double digit sales growth up to the turn of the century.
BRL's shares were up two cents at A$3.60 at 12.30 p.m.
